name: Gotion High-Tech Co., Ltd. (国轩高科股份有限公司)
founded: 2015 (listed vehicle — formerly Dongyuan Electric, renamed on the 2015 major asset restructuring)
employees: ~33,000 (implied: 4,358 R&D staff stated as 13.17% of headcount, 2025)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Gotion High-Tech's headline profit growth is almost entirely a securities revaluation, and the operating business behind it runs at a fraction of a percent of net margin — H1 2026 net profit attributable rose 278.05% to RMB 1,386.0m while profit excluding non-recurring items was RMB 106.9m on RMB 27,775.5m of revenue, a core net margin of 0.38%. It is simultaneously the only Chinese cell maker in this corpus with an operating US plant and the only one named on a US procurement blacklist, which is the tension the whole dossier turns on. BACKGROUND. The listed vehicle is Gotion High-Tech Co., Ltd., Shenzhen 002074, headquartered in Hefei, Anhui; it was formerly Dongyuan Electric and took its present shape in a 2015 major asset restructuring. Volkswagen (China) Investment is the largest shareholder at 24.28% and has not sold a share since 2021 — the percentage drift is dilution — but it contractually waives voting rights to sit at least five points below the founder party, and extended that waiver in December 2024 from 36 months to 72, to roughly December 2027. Li Zhen is the actual controller through a 17.85% concert party with his son and Nanjing Guoxuan Holding. FY2025 revenue was RMB 45,070.5m (+27.35%) on roughly 100 GWh of shipments; the company ranked fifth globally in EV battery installations at 4.5% share and ninth in storage cells at 4.5%.
ecosystemRole: Gotion reaches the AI-data-centre build-out from an angle no other Chinese cell maker in this corpus occupies: it claims to be the world's largest supplier of base-station and data-centre UPS backup batteries, above 28% share, and that claim appears in its own audited annual report rather than only in marketing. It also sells a containerised storage line — the Gotion Grid family at 5, 7 and 20 MWh, and a 5 MW / 18.8 MWh grid-forming cabinet — with a C&I product marketed explicitly at data centres. What it cannot do is sell any of that into a US project claiming a clean-energy tax credit. It is named on the FY2024 NDAA §154(b) list, which makes it a specified foreign entity by statute rather than by inference, and its US subsidiaries are captured with it, so the Manteno plant it actually operates in Illinois cannot claim the advanced manufacturing production credit for what it makes there. The Richardson Electronics partnership announced in May 2026 is the visible attempt to route around that.

productsAndServices.name: Power (EV) battery systems
productsAndServices.description: Gotion's largest segment at 75.6% of FY2025 revenue and 81.4% by H1 2026, spanning LFP, lithium manganese iron phosphate and ternary chemistries, and extended well beyond cars into electric vessels, low-altitude aircraft, power tools, two-wheelers and construction machinery.
highlights: The Qichen (启晨) LMFP line is the flagship: generation two is described by the company as the world's first ultra-fast-charge LMFP cell at 240 Wh/kg and 5C, and generation three launched at the May 2026 technology conference targeting passenger cars, vans and light and heavy trucks.

A fifth-generation LFP full-scenario cell reaches 205 Wh/kg, with a superfast variant charging 10–70% state of charge in under 4.5 minutes and an ultra-long-life variant carrying a 10-year vehicle warranty and a 30-year storage life.

G-Yuan is a hybrid solid-liquid cell at 300 Wh/kg with a stated 1,000 km vehicle range; the Gemstone all-solid-state cell claims 350 Wh/kg, has a 0.2 GWh pilot line commissioned in 2025 and entered on-road vehicle testing in March 2026.

Gnascent sodium-ion arrives in three variants — a 261 Wh/kg high-energy anode-free cell, a 162 Wh/kg power cell discharging to −50°C, and a 180Ah storage cell rated above 20,000 cycles — with gigawatt-scale lines at Tangshan and Hefei and mass production stated for Q4 2026.
The G-Xing heavy-truck standard pack is 116 kWh with four-gun parallel charging on a 1000V platform, and a modular building-block system performs a five-minute battery swap.
productsAndServices.positioning: Fifth globally in EV battery installations at 4.6% share in H1 2026, in a peer band with CALB and EVE Energy and far behind CATL and BYD, which hold 54.3% combined. In China it is fourth at roughly 6.3% and was passed by CALB during 2026.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Vehicle-programme nomination and direct supply. The company reports 100% direct sales — RMB 45.07bn, the whole of FY2025 revenue — with no distributor or licensing channel disclosed.

productsAndServices.name: Volkswagen unified cell programme
productsAndServices.description: A dedicated 20 GWh Hefei plant making Volkswagen's standard cell, in LFP and other chemistries, under a supply arrangement running 2026 to 2032. This is the single relationship that most distinguishes Gotion from its Chinese peers, and it is a customer relationship layered on top of a shareholding.
highlights: Mass production and a symbolic first delivery took place in Hefei in November 2025, received by Volkswagen's chief technology officer and PowerCo's chief executive.
Gotion won a new Volkswagen ID-series high-end nomination in H1 2026, and PowerCo now appears by name in the company's own customer list alongside VinFast, Rivian, Tata, Chery, Geely and Leapmotor.

The capital project behind it was repeatedly rescoped: from a 16 GWh high-energy-density line to a 20 GWh unified-cell line, with the implementing subsidiary changed, the in-service date pushed out, the project terminated early and the surplus proceeds permanently redirected to working capital.

Reported in July 2026 to be in talks to take a controlling stake in PowerCo's Sagunto plant near Valencia — 40 GWh initially, expandable to 60 GWh — with PowerCo stating on the record that it has no plans to relinquish control of the site.
Volkswagen holds 24.28% of Gotion and has two executives on its board, so the commercial and shareholding relationships are entangled in a way no peer's are.
productsAndServices.positioning: The anchor-OEM differentiator against CALB's GAC and Xpeng book and EVE's BMW cylindrical programme. Brokerage coverage treats scaled unified-cell deliveries from the second half of 2026 as the core growth driver for 2026–27.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct OEM supply under a long-term programme agreement.

productsAndServices.name: Energy storage systems — the Gotion Grid line
productsAndServices.description: A full-stack storage business running cells, standardised battery boxes, integrated cabinets and complete system solutions across generation-side, grid-side, commercial and industrial, residential and portable applications, certified to Chinese national standards plus UL, IEC, CSA and TÜV.
highlights: Gotion Grid 5 MWh is a liquid-cooled 20-foot unit holding temperature spread within 3°C on cells rated 12,000 cycles, with mass production started at Göttingen, Germany in July 2025 after certification under the EU Battery Regulation.
Gotion Grid 7 MWh carried more than 7 GWh of confirmed orders at its March 2025 launch; a 20 MWh modular system attracted more than 3 GWh of letters of intent at SNEC 2025.
The second-generation grid-forming system is a 5 MW / 18.8 MWh single cabin integrating batteries, inverters and controls in one enclosure at 92.1% efficiency, with an embedded lightweight AI model.

Qianyuan Zaidao is the commercial and industrial product, configurable at two or four hours above 91% round-trip efficiency, and marketed explicitly for industrial parks, PV-storage-charging stations, data centres and microgrids.

Named projects include the Baotou Weijun 1.2 GWh grid-side station in China, two Japanese storage stations, and Lightsource bp's Lower Wonga in Queensland at 281 MW / 843 MWh paired with a 380 MWdc solar plant.
productsAndServices.positioning: Ninth globally in storage cell shipments at 4.5% for H1 2026 and losing about a point of share, in a field where Great Power is growing five times faster off a similar base. Research houses disagree sharply on the FY2025 rank — EVTank places Gotion eighth, ICC has it in the top ten, and InfoLink does not name it in its top six at all.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Project tendering, large-customer strategic cooperation and direct system integration. Overseas sales skew to integrated systems and domestic sales to bare cells.

productsAndServices.name: Base-station and data-centre UPS backup batteries
productsAndServices.description: The company's strongest stated market position and the one most directly relevant to this corpus: Gotion reports being ranked first globally in base-station and data-centre uninterruptible-power-supply backup batteries, with share above 28%, citing ICC. Products are specified at 6C high-rate discharge and a 15-year design service life.
highlights: The 28% figure appears in the audited FY2025 annual report's market-position discussion, not only in a press release — which makes it a harder claim than most data-centre positioning in this sector.
It is nonetheless a share statistic attributed to a single research house, and no independent research house reached in this session publishes a base-station or UPS backup category at all.

AI data-centre storage is named in the H1 2026 filing as forming a new growth pole driving continued market expansion, and data centres appear in the annual report's list of emerging storage scenarios alongside mining.
Collection gap: no named data-centre operator, hyperscaler, colocation provider or UPS original-equipment manufacturer appears in any source. The share is stated; the counterparties are not.
For contrast, the AI-data-centre storage orders that did surface in the same window went to other suppliers — Energy Vault at 1.25 GW and ERock at 470 MW.
productsAndServices.positioning: If the 28% figure holds, Gotion is the leading supplier in a category the major research houses do not track — which is why it cannot be corroborated and should be carried as a company claim.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to telecom operators and data-centre builders; not broken out in segment reporting.

productsAndServices.name: Materials, resources and recycling
productsAndServices.description: An unusually deep vertical position for a cell maker, spanning mining and beneficiation, cathode, anode, separator, electrolyte, copper foil and precursors, plus a closed-loop recycling network.
highlights: Resource positions at the Yichun lithium mine in Jiangxi, Indonesian nickel, and Argentine salt-lake lithium held as a resource interest rather than an operating stake.
A 200,000 tonne per year LFP cathode project under construction, carried at RMB 657.0m of construction in progress at 30 June 2026.
The world's first zero-carbon anode-material plant, commissioned at Wuhai in Inner Mongolia.
A memorandum with BASF signed February 2026 on high-performance materials for next-generation solid-state batteries.
A solid-state materials roadmap targeting 300 tonnes per year of lithium sulfide and 2,000 tonnes of solid electrolyte by 2026, scaling to 50,000 and 100,000 tonnes by 2030.
productsAndServices.positioning: Vertical integration is Gotion's answer to per-watt-hour cost compression in the Chinese second tier, where it competes with CALB, EVE and SVOLT rather than with CATL.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Largely captive, feeding its own cell plants.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess Gotion's reported profit growth materially overstates the operating business, and that the gap is structural rather than a one-off. Basis: H1 2026 net profit attributable of RMB 1,386.0m against ex-non-recurring profit of RMB 106.9m — 92.3% non-recurring — on revenue of RMB 27,775.5m, a 0.38% core net margin. Fair-value changes were 72.35% of total profit, grants 26.44%. The same shape held at FY2025 (+97.49% headline, RMB 431.8m ex-non-recurring), Q1 2026 was down 79.04%, and Q4 2025 was a loss quarter on the year's largest revenue. In August 2026 the board authorised further listed-equity disposals up to 15% of net assets, so the mechanism is mandated to continue.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess Gotion is the most US-exposed and most US-constrained Chinese cell maker in this corpus at the same time, and that this is the defining fact about it. Basis: it is the only one with an operating US plant — five lines at Manteno, Illinois, on more than USD 536m of pledged state incentives — and it is named in NDAA §154(b), making it a specified foreign entity by statute rather than by inference. Its US subsidiaries are captured with it, so the plant it actually runs cannot claim the advanced manufacturing production credit for what it makes. It also carries the stranded capital its peers avoided: USD 2.4bn at Big Rapids, written off after Michigan declared default.

3. **(High confidence)** We assess three widely repeated claims about Gotion's US legal position are false and should be corrected wherever the corpus repeats them. Basis: it is NOT on the UFLPA Entity List as of the 31 July 2026 update despite a congressional demand that it be added; it is NOT on the Department of Defense §1260H list as of 8 June 2026, unlike CATL, BYD, CALB and EVE, so it escapes the §805 contracting bans that catch them; and the NO GOTION Act was never enacted — H.R. 524 sits at 'introduced' with no further action. Separately, the §30D framing that drove all 2023–24 coverage is moot, because §30D itself terminated for vehicles acquired after 30 September 2025.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess Volkswagen's position is a control question with a dated trigger, not a static shareholding. Basis: Volkswagen (China) Investment holds 24.28% on an unchanged 440,630,983 shares — the drift from 26.47% is dilution, not a sale — but it contractually waives voting rights to sit at least five points below the founder party, and in December 2024 extended that waiver from 36 months to 72, to approximately 15 December 2027. Li Zhen remains actual controller on a 17.85% concert party. The waiver also lapses if Volkswagen's stake falls below 15%, and the approved but uncompleted RMB 5.0bn placement is a live dilution path. Commentary still describing a 'three-year' waiver is working from the expired original term.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess the storage business is losing ground while the EV business gains it, and that the company's disclosure obscures which. Basis: EV installations rose 43.3% in H1 2026 to hold fifth globally, while storage share fell about a point to 4.5% and ninth, with Great Power growing five times faster off a similar base. More sharply, SNE reports Gotion's H1 2026 storage shipments up 41% while the company's own storage revenue fell 19.14% — a divergence the filing calls 'business structure optimisation' and does not reconcile. Either severe price erosion or a shift from systems to bare cells; both readings are unfavourable to margin.

6. **(Low confidence)** We assess the data-centre backup position is Gotion's most valuable strategic asset and its least verifiable claim. Basis: the audited FY2025 annual report states above 28% global share and first place in base-station and data-centre UPS backup batteries, citing ICC — appearing in a filing rather than only in marketing, which is a higher bar than most sector positioning clears. Against that, no independent research house reached in this session publishes such a category at all, so the figure cannot be corroborated, and no named data-centre operator, hyperscaler or UPS manufacturer appears anywhere. Collection gap: the share is stated, the counterparties are absent.

policyExposure.exposure: Gotion is a specified foreign entity on two independent statutory grounds, which is what separates it from every other Chinese cell maker in this corpus. It is named on the FY2024 NDAA §154(b) list imported by 26 U.S.C. §7701(a)(51)(B)(iv), and it is separately a PRC-incorporated foreign-controlled entity under clause (B)(v); its US subsidiaries are captured as controlled entities. Two distinct prohibitions follow and are frequently conflated: no Gotion entity may claim §45X, §45Y, §48E, §45Q, §45U or §45Z for taxable years beginning after 4 July 2025, and separately a §45X eligible component containing any material assistance from a prohibited foreign entity is disqualified outright. A US storage project using Gotion cells must additionally clear a 55% material assistance cost ratio in 2026, rising to 75% after 2029 — a test whose worked example in IRS Notice 2026-15 fails at 27.2%. New §6662(m) drops the substantial-understatement threshold to 1% and §6501(o) extends the assessment window to six years, which is why developers avoid the question rather than argue it.
policyExposure.mitigation: The Richardson Electronics partnership announced 13 May 2026 is the visible attempt at a workaround — Gotion supplies technology from Manteno and Richardson handles commercialisation and integration from La Fox, Illinois, on a 760 kWh commercial product and a 5 MWh utility product. Neither party has published a credit-eligibility claim, and the statutory 'effective control' prong that would govern such a licensing structure has no Treasury definition yet.

policyExposure.regime: NDAA §154 Department of Defense procurement ban
policyExposure.exposure: Gotion High-tech is one of exactly six entities named in §154(b) of the FY2024 National Defense Authorization Act, alongside CATL, BYD, Envision Energy, EVE Energy and Hithium. From 1 October 2027 the Department of Defense may not procure its batteries. The ban is prospective and confined to Defense procurement — it is not a government-wide bar and no FAR-level prohibition was located.
policyExposure.mitigation: None available. Being named is not curable by restructuring.

policyExposure.exposure: Three widely repeated claims fail on checking, and the corrections matter. Gotion is NOT on the UFLPA Entity List as of the 31 July 2026 update, despite a June 2024 congressional demand that it be added. It is NOT on the Department of Defense §1260H Chinese military companies list as of the 8 June 2026 update — unlike CATL, BYD, CALB and EVE — so it escapes the §805 contracting bans that catch those peers. And the NO GOTION Act was never enacted: H.R. 6175 died in the 118th Congress and H.R. 524, reintroduced 16 January 2025, remains at 'introduced' with no further action. No CFIUS proceeding has ever been publicly confirmed, only demanded.
policyExposure.mitigation: Not applicable — these are absences rather than exposures, recorded because the corpus and the trade press both tend to assume the opposite.

policyExposure.regime: US state-level incentive clawback and local litigation
policyExposure.exposure: Michigan declared Gotion in default on the Big Rapids project on 17 September 2025 after more than 120 days without eligible construction activity, terminating about USD 175m of incentives of which only the USD 23.6m land purchase had been disbursed. The state attorney general demanded repayment of USD 23.7m in January 2026 and Gotion refused in February, arguing the land had been rendered undevelopable. In May 2026 Gotion Inc. sued Green Charter Township for damages, itemising sunk costs of USD 24m land, USD 56m salaries and infrastructure, USD 7.3m architecture and engineering and USD 0.5m management. Separately in Illinois, a citizens' suit over the Manteno rezoning survived partial dismissal and proceeded toward trial, and Manteno trustees voted 3–2 in January 2026 against asking Gotion to make a voluntary CFIUS filing.
policyExposure.mitigation: Manteno is operating and Gotion closed out the fire-readiness items its local fire chief raised, standing up a site brigade and an approved emergency action plan by January 2026. The Michigan project is not recoverable.

policyExposure.exposure: Moot, and recorded because it is the single most out-of-date framing in circulation. The FEOC test under §30D drove essentially all 2023 and 2024 coverage of Gotion's US position — the argument that its cells would disqualify a vehicle from the USD 7,500 credit. OBBBA terminated §30D for vehicles acquired after 30 September 2025, so there is no longer a credit for the test to attach to.

relationships.note: Ninth against sixth in global storage cell shipments for H1 2026 — Gotion 20.8 GWh and 4.5%, REPT 31.4 GWh and 6.8%. Covered together as the corpus's paired study of how US foreign-entity rules bear on Chinese cell makers.
relationships.context: The pair is the point. To a US buyer's tax-credit arithmetic they are equally disqualifying — both are prohibited foreign entities. On every other axis they diverge sharply: Gotion is named in NDAA §154(b) with a Defense procurement ban dated 1 October 2027, has an operating Illinois plant and an abandoned Michigan one with incentives clawed back, and carries live state-level political exposure. REPT is named on no list, has no US plant and no stranded capital.

relationships.note: A different weight class in both markets — 39.9% of global EV battery installations and 27.1% of storage cells in H1 2026, against Gotion's 4.6% and 4.5%.
relationships.context: Also a peer on the §154(b) list, and unlike Gotion, additionally on the Department of Defense §1260H list since January 2025 — so CATL carries the §805 contracting bans that Gotion escapes.

relationships.note: Second globally in EV batteries at 14.4% and fourth in storage cells at 7.7% for H1 2026.
relationships.context: Named in §154(b) alongside Gotion and added to the §1260H list at parent level in June 2026. The comparison that matters is captive consumption: BYD consumes its own cells in its own vehicles, Gotion sells to Volkswagen and others.

relationships.note: Directly adjacent in both markets — seventh in EV installations at 3.4% and second in storage cells at 10.4% for H1 2026, where it is well ahead of Gotion.
relationships.context: Named in §154(b) and added to §1260H in June 2026. Among Chinese peers, EVE's storage position is the one Gotion has most clearly lost ground against.

relationships.note: Third globally in storage cells at 10.0% for H1 2026, more than double Gotion's share in a market Gotion entered earlier.
relationships.context: Also named in §154(b). Hithium is the storage-specialised comparison; Gotion's storage business is a second line behind EV batteries and is losing share while Hithium's grows.

relationships.note: Eighth in global storage cell shipments for H1 2026 through its AESC arm, just ahead of Gotion.
relationships.context: The sixth and final name on the §154(b) list. Envision's response to the material-assistance rules was to sell its Tennessee cell plant to a US buyer — a structural exit from the problem that Gotion has not attempted.

relationships.note: Tenth globally in EV battery installations at 2.4% for H1 2026, inside the same Chinese second tier as Gotion, CALB and EVE.
relationships.context: Notably absent from the §154(b) list, which is the axis on which this peer group genuinely diverges.

relationships.note: Twelfth in global storage cell shipments at 1.4% for H1 2026 — a Korean comparator whose value here is as the non-Chinese alternative a US buyer reaches for precisely because of the foreign-entity rules.
relationships.context: The Korean and Japanese suppliers are the direct beneficiaries of the material-assistance regime that constrains Gotion.

relationships.note: Third in global EV battery installations at 8.6% and eleventh in storage cells at 2.6% for H1 2026, with storage shipments up 357% year on year.
relationships.context: The clearest illustration of the policy tailwind: a non-Chinese supplier growing storage shipments more than fourfold in the year the US rules tightened around Chinese cells.

relationships.note: Supplying the Lower Wonga solar-plus-storage project in Queensland, Australia — 281 MW / 843 MWh paired with a 380 MWdc solar plant, through an engineering joint venture with INTEC, with commercial operation targeted for late 2028.
relationships.context: The clearest named storage customer on the record, and it sits in Australia rather than the US or Europe. Lightsource bp's own dossier records the same project from the buyer's side and notes that its US book is deliberately kept clear of Chinese storage suppliers — so this relationship exists precisely where the US foreign-entity rules do not reach.

relationships.note: A storage-system competitor, and the company whose dossier already cites Gotion as a cautionary precedent — that a US plant alone does not guarantee tax-credit eligibility.
relationships.context: That inbound characterisation is correct and this session's research strengthens it: Gotion's Manteno plant operates, and its output still cannot claim §45X, because prohibited-foreign-entity status attaches to the owner rather than the site.

relationships.note: A Chinese supplier in the telecom and data-centre backup power segment, which is where Gotion claims its strongest position — above 28% global share and first place in base-station and data-centre UPS backup batteries.
relationships.context: Recorded because that segment is the one most relevant to this corpus and the one no major research house independently tracks; Gotion's share claim rests on a single house and cannot be corroborated.

periods.commentary: The auditor made receivables recoverability a key audit matter and separately flagged the inherent risk that management manipulates revenue recognition to meet targets. Quarterly net profit attributable ran RMB 100.6m, RMB 266.0m, RMB 2,166.6m and RMB −150.0m: the third quarter carried the year and the fourth was a loss on the largest revenue quarter.

periods.commentary: Unaudited interim. Consensus is wide and unreliable: a thirteen-institution aggregation priced 2 September 2026 forecasts FY2026 net profit of RMB 1,847m, while a June 2026 brokerage initiation forecasts RMB 968m — a roughly twofold spread. Neither is reconcilable with an H1 ex-non-recurring result of RMB 106.9m without a very large second half or continued portfolio gains.

financials.commentary: Gotion reports only in RMB and offers no USD translation of revenue or profit anywhere in its filings; the USD overlays above are conversions at a cited 2025 average rate. The single most important reading instruction for this record is to use the 扣非 (excluding non-recurring items) line rather than the headline — the two have diverged by roughly an order of magnitude in each of the last three reported periods.
